claim: The recreated SDK's pre-login readiness failure published one bounded local observation that matched exactly one redacted Loki record by observation_id and receipt_id. Current Prometheus targets were healthy.

correlation.method: Exactly one observation JSON file within five seconds of the readiness receipt matched its status, configured_model, duration_ms, usage_status and null usage. Its file mtime equalled the readiness receipt mtime; its opaque observation_id was used in the bounded native Loki query.

native_commands.purpose: Query only the identified observation in its bounded time window
Read current scrape-target health and summarize only counts

parameter_scope.LOKI_URL: The configured local Loki HTTP endpoint
parameter_scope.PROMETHEUS_URL: The configured local Prometheus HTTP endpoint
parameter_scope.OBSERVATION_ID: Private observation_id from the uniquely correlated bounded SDK observation

limitations: This preserves the earlier pre-login failed readiness run. It is not a statement of the current account state after the subsequent successful native sign-in.
This proves local failure visibility and current scrape health, not successful native model inference or complete Codex/Claude runtime E2E.
Failed-run token usage is unknown, not zero. The helper explicitly recorded that no model inference was submitted.

The readiness receipt lacks a persisted observation_id; correlation therefore combines a unique bounded-time local candidate with exact metadata agreement, followed by exact private-ID matching in Loki.
The configured collector receipt format intentionally omits the raw error and retains status/usage metadata; authentication classification comes from the private native readiness receipt.
No general conversations, authentication stores or service-configuration secrets were read. No service changes, account probes or model calls were made for this check.
